title: Recursive Self-Evolving Agents via Held-Out Selection
mutable_substrate: A compact injected natural-language state with three rewritable layers: an imperative strategy, reusable skills/conditional subroutines, and a procedural playbook. The ReAct scaffold, tools, and LLM weights are frozen.
optimization_operator: Across generations, the current state is rolled out on a disjoint evolve set; the same frozen LLM acts as meta-optimizer and holistically rewrites or drops content in all three layers from balanced successful and failed trajectories. RSEA_R optionally combines the frozen cross-task prior with Reflexion-style per-task retries.
feedback_selection: Environment-verified success selects candidates on ALFWorld and tau-bench; WebShop uses dense benchmark reward. A candidate may become the working state if it does not regress versus the current state on held-out validation, while the frozen best state updates only on a strict validation improvement over the recorded best initialized to empty-state ReAct.
archive_memory: The persistent memory is the bounded three-layer natural-language state plus a separately frozen best state. Rewrites may delete entries, preventing append-only context growth; no population archive or code repository lineage is used.
validation_strategy: Disjoint evolve/validation/evaluation splits; only the frozen best state reaches test. ALFWorld uses 134 test tasks across five seeds with paired McNemar on matched task-seed cells; GAIA, tau-bench, and WebShop use one seed-shuffled split with 30/60/100 eval tasks. The study reimplements six baselines on shared local backbones and includes state-layer and no-held-out-gate ablations.
adaptation_mode: Offline cross-task natural-language evolution over a fixed development pool, followed by frozen single-pass inference; RSEA_R adds within-task retry. It is not online continual deployment and does not update weights, tools, code, or topology.
benchmarks: ALFWorld: 134 balanced test tasks x 5 seeds plus a disjoint 30-task development pool; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; environment success
GAIA v1 Level-1 text: 30 tasks with live search/fetch/Python tools; Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct; official accuracy
tau-bench retail: 60 held-out evaluation tasks with an LLM user simulator and DB-hash success; Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct
WebShop: 100 held-out tasks over a 1,000-product subset with Lucene retrieval; Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct; dense grounded-shopping score
principal_results: On ALFWorld, single-pass RSEA scores 69.3% +/- 9.3 versus ReAct 64.6% +/- 4.3 (paired McNemar p=0.015), GEPA 63.9% (p=0.004), and AWM 65.4% (p=0.037); it is tied with ACE 66.9% and Dynamic Cheatsheet 70.7%.
RSEA_R reaches 79.4% +/- 7.4 on ALFWorld, significantly above ReAct and single-pass RSEA (p<1e-4) but not significantly above Reflexion 76.4%, ACE_R 76.7%, or GEPA_R 75.8%.
AWM leads the strong-backbone tool tasks at 51.7% tau-bench success and 0.460 WebShop score; RSEA scores 40.0% and 0.437, statistically tied with ReAct at 41.7% and 0.429.
Dynamic Cheatsheet scores 70.7% on ALFWorld but collapses to 36.7% on tau-bench and 0.136 on WebShop, illustrating the risk of unguarded online context.
The no-held-out-gate RSEA ablation attains 100.0% on its in-sample selection set but 66.7% test success, a 33.3-point train-test gap; strict RSEA scores 67.3%, only 0.6 points higher on test.
Individual layer ablations score 67.3% strategy-only and 69.8% skills-only/playbook-only versus 64.2% empty; full RSEA scores 68.5%, showing overlapping rather than additive layers.
RSEA improves tau-bench held-out validation from 0.20 to 0.36 but test success is numerically below ReAct, demonstrating that validation monotonicity does not guarantee test improvement.
limitations: The strict gate guarantees non-regression only on the repeatedly reused empirical validation split, not on the test distribution or every task subgroup.

RSEA is numerically below ReAct on GAIA (13.3 vs 16.7) and tau-bench (40.0 vs 41.7), although neither difference is statistically significant; 'never regresses' must be read as 'never significantly underperforms.'
Repeatedly comparing adaptively generated candidates on one small validation set can overfit validation; no nested selection, sequential correction, or validation-size study is reported.
Transfer benchmarks use one shuffled split seed and small evaluation sets; GAIA live-web noise flips the sign of a one-task difference across runs.
Only ReAct and RSEA are reported on GAIA, so the six-baseline study is not a complete benchmark-by-method factorial comparison.
The isolated strict-versus-no-gate ALFWorld test difference is only 0.6 points with no significance test; Dynamic Cheatsheet differs from RSEA in form and update schedule as well as its missing gate.
The state layers are not additive: full state underperforms skills-only and playbook-only on the reported ablation subset.
The paper excludes code-, tool-, topology-, and weight-updating self-improvement and under-specifies several per-benchmark search hyperparameters and full compute cost.
safety_controls: Proposal trajectories, validation tasks, and final evaluation tasks are disjoint.
The frozen best state is initialized to empty-state ReAct and updates only on strict held-out validation improvement; ties preserve the simpler fallback.
A candidate may move the exploratory working state laterally but cannot overwrite the frozen release state without a strict gain.
Only the frozen best state is evaluated on test, preventing direct test leakage into selection.
State entries are required to be short, transferable, and instance-agnostic, and rewrites may delete content to prevent unbounded context growth.
Shared local backbones, identical task/rewrite models, common budgets, preregistered manifests, and per-task results support auditability.

explicit_predecessors.name: ReAct
explicit_predecessors.evidence: RSEA keeps the ReAct loop unchanged, injects only the evolved preamble, initializes the best state to empty ReAct, and uses ReAct as the primary paired baseline.

explicit_predecessors.name: Reflexion
explicit_predecessors.relationship: Within-task adaptation predecessor composed with RSEA in the RSEA_R variant.
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Background contrasts Reflexion's per-task retries with cross-task evolution; RSEA_R explicitly injects the frozen prior into a Reflexion-style multi-trial loop.

explicit_predecessors.name: GEPA
explicit_predecessors.relationship: Flat-prompt evolutionary predecessor and validation-selected baseline.
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The method taxonomy names GEPA's reflective mutation and Pareto selection on validation minibatches, and ALFWorld/tau-bench/WebShop results compare it directly.

explicit_predecessors.name: Agent Workflow Memory (AWM)
explicit_predecessors.relationship: Concrete workflow-induction predecessor and strongest transfer baseline.
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The taxonomy defines AWM as inducing workflow lists from successes; it leads tau-bench and WebShop and establishes the scope condition favoring concrete procedures on detailed tool APIs.

explicit_predecessors.name: Agentic Context Engineering (ACE)
explicit_predecessors.relationship: Add-only playbook predecessor with non-strict validation keep-best.
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The taxonomy explicitly contrasts ACE's bullet playbook/add-only deltas/non-strict validation rule with RSEA's holistic three-layer rewrite and strict best update.

explicit_predecessors.name: Dynamic Cheatsheet
explicit_predecessors.relationship: Unguarded online-context predecessor used as the principal negative comparison for held-out release discipline.
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The taxonomy identifies no held-out gate; experiments show 70.7% on ALFWorld but 0.136 WebShop and 36.7% tau-bench performance.

explicit_predecessors.name: Automated Design of Agentic Systems (ADAS)
explicit_predecessors.relationship: Explicitly cited adjacent self-evolution approach that searches agent code/topology rather than natural-language state.
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Related Work explicitly contrasts searching over agent code/topology with RSEA's weight-frozen, natural-language-state evolution.

open_questions: How should held-out selection correct for many adaptively proposed generations evaluated on the same validation set?
What validation size and composition are required for reliable non-regression under task-family imbalance or distribution shift?
Can subgroup-aware release constraints prevent aggregate validation gains from hiding regressions such as ALFWorld clean tasks?
Should a deployment evaluator remain fixed for comparability or co-evolve to track changing task distributions, and how can evaluator drift remain safe?
Would uncertainty-aware, sequential, or Bayesian selection outperform strict point-estimate keep-better on small validation sets?
How does the release rule transfer to executable code, tool, topology, or weight updates where candidate failures can have side effects beyond benchmark score?
What is the full cost-effectiveness once evolve rollouts, validation rollouts, rewrite tokens, retry calls, wall-clock, and GPU-hours are counted?
